title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 95 (Registers to be evidence)

content.overview: Registers and copies of returns kept under sections 88 and 94 are prima facie evidence of the matters directed or authorised to be inserted in them. The evidentiary effect is prima facie, not conclusive.
content.glance: Registers and copies of returns kept under sections 88 and 94 are prima facie evidence of the matters directed or authorised to be inserted in them. The evidentiary effect is prima facie, not conclusive.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 95 (Registers to be evidence). The registers and copies of returns kept under sections 88 and 94 are prima facie evidence of the matters directed or authorised to be inserted in them. The provision gives those records evidentiary value but does not state that every entry is conclusive or immune from challenge. Questions about correcting or rectifying an entry must be addressed under the applicable substantive procedure, including section 59 where relevant. The topic remains under source and current-law review.

sections.heading: Covered records
sections.body: Section 95 applies to registers and copies of returns kept under sections 88 and 94.

sections.heading: Evidentiary effect
sections.body: Those registers and copies of returns are prima facie evidence of the matters directed or authorised to be inserted in them.

sections.heading: Limit
sections.body: Prima facie evidence is not the same as conclusive proof. Section 95 does not itself prescribe a separate rectification procedure.

hypotheticals.question: A party relies on an entry in a register maintained under section 88. What evidentiary effect does section 95 give the register?
hypotheticals.analysis: The register and copies of returns kept under sections 88 and 94 are prima facie evidence of matters directed or authorised to be inserted. Do not describe the entry as conclusive proof solely because section 95 applies.

hypotheticals.question: Does section 95 itself provide the procedure to rectify an incorrect entry?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 95 states an evidentiary rule. Any rectification issue must be considered under the applicable substantive provision and procedure, such as section 59 where relevant.

distinctions.title: Prima facie evidence and conclusive proof
distinctions.left: Section 95 gives prima facie evidentiary effect to the registers and returns identified in sections 88 and 94.
distinctions.right: A challenge to an entry or a request for rectification must be considered under the applicable substantive provision and procedure.

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 95 as making every register entry conclusive.
misconceptions.correction: The section gives prima facie evidentiary effect only.

misconceptions.trap: Applying section 95 to any company record without checking sections 88 and 94.
misconceptions.correction: Identify whether the record is a register or copy of a return kept under the provisions named by section 95.

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 95 itself as a rectification mechanism.
misconceptions.correction: Use the applicable rectification provision where correction of an entry is sought.
